name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council harmonising certain aspects of insolvency law
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on common minimum rules for insolvency across the EU. It aims to make outcomes more predictable for creditors and investors, so cross-border lending and investment are less risky. It tightens rules for undoing unfair pre-insolvency deals, gives insolvency practitioners better access to bank account and ownership registers, adds safeguards for selling a failing business as a going concern, and requires company directors to file for insolvency within three months of becoming aware of insolvency. It removes the Commission's special rules for microenterprises.

- **What changes:** Common EU minimum standards on challenging unfair deals, tracing assets, pre-pack sales and directors' filing duties.
- **Who it affects:** Creditors, investors, company directors, insolvency practitioners and workers across the EU.
- **What happens next:** Parliament's first-reading position goes to EU governments for negotiation; national laws follow once agreed.
